newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hopes for Russian Paris Club participation.
newsitem.headline: France hopes for Russian Paris Club participation.

text.p: France and Russia said on Tuesday they hoped for an early agreement which would allow Moscow to participate in the Paris Club of creditor nations.

"We are pleased to see that discussions between Russia and creditor nations to decide the conditions under which Russia can participate in this body as a creditor are advancing," French Prime Minister Alain Juppe told a news conference.
"France would like the discussions to be completed as soon as possible," he said after a meeting with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Russia, which as a debtor nation signed a long-term rescheduling agreement with the Paris Club earlier this year, has said it also wants to join as a creditor.
Membership of the Paris Club would allow it to negotiate the return of Soviet-era debts owed to Moscow, mainly by developing countries.

"I must say that we can be pleased by the fact that negotiations are currently taking place between Russia and creditor nations in the Paris Club to try to define conditions which would allow Russia to participate in the Paris Club as a creditor," Chernomyrdin told the news conference.
"We would like to express our wishes to see these negotiations end as quickly as possible and we hope that this will be the case," he added.
France and Russia earlier signed an agreement allowing for some repayment to French bondholders of tsarist debt issued before the 1917 Russian Revolution.
A dispute between the two countries over the tsarist debt had been cited by some as one obstacle to Russia's membership of the Paris Club.
A bigger obstacle, however, has been over how to translate loans made by Moscow in roubles many years ago into today's exchange rates.
Paris Club chairman Christian Noyer has previously suggested Russia could participate informally in Paris Club talks, particularly given the volume of debt owed to Moscow by developing countries.
The Paris Club has pledged to improve debt relief available to the world's poorest, heavily indebted countries.
